previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with end-stage renal disease, diastolic heart failure, and atrial fibrillation was admitted after developing acute dyspnea and palpitations when lying down, following a recent hospitalization for post-dialysis hypotension. She presented with severe hypertension and hypoxia, requiring BiPAP and intravenous nitroglycerin. Imaging revealed pulmonary edema and right-sided lung consolidation, initially concerning for pneumonia, but clinical improvement favored heart failure as the primary cause. She was restarted on antihypertensive therapy with metoprolol, lisinopril, and valsartan, held on dialysis days to prevent hypotension. A urine culture grew Klebsiella pneumoniae, prompting treatment with Bactrim dosed around dialysis. Her INR rose to 4.0 due to drug interaction, leading to temporary discontinuation of warfarin. She also reported left eye pain from glaucoma, managed with analgesia and continued eye drops. After two dialysis sessions and clinical stabilization, she was discharged home in good condition, breathing comfortably on room air with controlled blood pressure and instructions for close follow-up.

Brief Hospital Course:
This is a ___ year old woman admitted with respiratory failure 
likely from acute-on-chronic diastolic heart failure, initially 
managed in the MICU then transferred to the floor after 
hemodialysis and resolution in respiratory failure.

# Respiratory failure: Very likely from acute-on-chronic 
diastolic CHF, also with question of underlying infectious 
pulmonary process. Patient improved quickly after emergent 
hemodialysis for volume control and BP control to help reduce 
afterload. Given poor evidence for underlying PNA on imaging, 
afebrile, and only isolated leukocytosis, vancomycin was 
discontinued in MICU, but an empiric course of levofloxacin for 
pneumonia which was started in the ED was continued. Influenza 
DFA and urine Legionella antigen were negative. Patient received 
influenza vaccine prior to discharge. Patient also received a 
second round of ultrafilration on the day of discharge with plan 
to resume outpatient hemodialysis on her regular 
___ schedule.
  
# Leukocytosis: Etiologies included UTI vs. possible PNA vs. 
acute stress reaction. Urine culture grew out enterococcus. 
Blood cultures from admission negative at time of discharge. 
Patient was continued on empiric coverage with levofloxacin 
which also would cover majority of enterococcus with 
leukocytosis resolved at time of discharge.
  
# Chronic Kidneay Disease V on hemodialysis: Patient received 
emergent hemodialysis on admission w/ ~ 3L Ultra Filtration 
removed. Patient was continued on phosphate binders. She 
received a last run of hemodialysis on day of discharge. Patient 
to resume regular schedule on ___ at ___.

admissions for similar complaint. During this admission, some 
suggestion of blood pressure medication verses dietary

adequate blood pressure control. Three sets of cardiac enzymes 
were negative. She was continued on aspirin.  

# DM2: She was continued on home insulin NPH with sliding scale 
and aspirin with adequate control of blood sugars. 
  
# Atrial fibrillation: On presentation, she was in sinus rhythm 
with INR therapeutic. Her home beta blocker and amiodarone and

antibiotic use. Patient to have INR checked on ___ with HD.
